representative_tasks.task: LoRA fine-tune a 7B model on 40 labeled examples
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Flags overfitting risk; suggests few-shot/augmentation first; if training, a held-out split, low rank, few epochs and early stopping

representative_tasks.task: Prepare an instruction dataset and train a LoRA adapter
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Adapter trained with completion-only loss and a held-out eval split

negative_cases: Request to fine-tune to inject frequently-changing facts better served by retrieval (planned)
rubric: Dataset-size risk flagged before any recipe
prerequisites: example-deps (torch, transformers, peft, trl, datasets, tokenizers) for executable tests; no model download (from_pretrained is patched to a tiny random Llama)
execution_constraints: Offline grading and fixture self-tests need only Python 3.10+ stdlib and no network.
Executable tests need the example-test dependencies (see docs/EXAMPLE-TESTS.md) and run via run_evals.py --run-executable.
Model-mode runs need --provider anthropic --model <id> --allow-network and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; they cost money and are not deterministic.
expected_artifacts: Train/held-out eval split of a prompt/completion dataset wired into the SFT trainer
LoRA adapter and merged model directories (written in a temp dir by the example test)
known_limitations: Hard assertions are regexes over the response text: they verify that key concepts are stated, not that the reasoning connecting them is correct.
No baseline (with-skill vs without-skill) has been measured for this skill; any uplift claim requires a recorded or model run.
No case trains a real model; the example tests use tiny stubbed models.
Executable tests use fakes or tiny local models instead of real services/checkpoints (see each case's limitations); they prove the skill's published code paths, not a model response.
unsupported_use_cases: Grounding in a corpus at inference time (rag-pipeline)
